question: Hyperkalaemia with ECG changes is an absolute indication for emergency renal replacement therapy in AKI, even if the patient is still passing some urine.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The AEIOU indications for emergency RRT include hyperkalaemia that is refractory to medical treatment or associated with ECG changes (peaked T-waves, wide QRS, sine-wave). This is an emergency regardless of urine output volume.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The AEIOU indications for emergency RRT are: Acidosis (pH <7.1 refractory), Electrolytes (hyperkalaemia refractory or with ECG changes), Intoxication (dialysable toxins), Oedema (pulmonary, refractory), Uraemia (encephalopathy, pericarditis). ECG changes indicate imminent cardiac arrest risk — dialysis is mandatory regardless of urine output.
